task_contract.objective: Produce readable C++ whose compiled function exactly matches the assigned target using the official MSVC9 compiler, original pack and flags.
task_contract.inputs: The assignment supplies the claim directory, independent work directory, target address, size, model, checker budget and versioned resource_paths. Read claim.json, packet.json, pack/pack.json, relevant source neighbourhood, and the compiler tips, official guidance and checker README from those resource paths. Treat upstream guidance as reference material within this assignment’s scope and permissions. Extract target instructions locally from the game image identified by the assignment's resource_paths.game_image using the existing Python tools. Parse large index/symbol files in code and retrieve only relevant entries.
task_contract.execution: Use the assignment’s recorded checker commands for all candidate checks and diagnostic compilations. The controller selects the official checker generation and applies its environment after the environment script identified by the assignment's resource_paths.environment_script. Request exec_command sandbox_permissions=require_escalated for compiler runs or authorized writes outside sandbox roots. On approval rejection, stop and report. Count every compiler invocation, including diagnostics, toward the assigned budget using the recorder’s conservative accounting. Stop at the first actual plain MATCH or the budget. No generated program execution.
task_contract.source_rules: Emit the complete assigned function with only the minimal additional declarations it requires. The checker supplies the original unit and headers; use their declared types and symbols. Official pack/compiler/checker/image/flags remain unchanged. Real named-field C++ only; no asm, naked functions, raw bytes, absolute-address tricks, filler arrays or preprocessor workarounds. Keep original game bytes/disassembly in local files. Work only in assigned work directory and the collaboration paths explicitly listed by the assignment, with read-only assigned pack and toolchain. No secrets, network or service/API operations. Read other workers' candidates only when the assignment identifies them as members of the same collaboration group and supplies their shared paths.
task_contract.outputs: Retain each candidate revision, its source SHA256 and complete checker log. Save result.json with model, match boolean, final_candidate_path, checker_invocations and concise residual_issue. On failure retain the closest actually checked source, not simply the last variant. Use complete results and code; keep progress brief.
task_contract.defects: Save defect-proposal.json only when checked evidence establishes a data or tool defect that prevents a valid solution under the assignment's permitted source rules, original pack, compiler and flags. Include a concise factual note, reproduction evidence, and why permitted source changes cannot resolve the blocker. Difficulty, exhausted attempts, diagnostic quirks, naming ambiguities with a valid workaround, and unproven compiler-flag hypotheses are not established blockers. Preserve those observations in the handoff instead. Only the operator may decide whether to flag a function.
task_contract.attempts: Use the batch-round allowance specified in the assignment. A round may contain 1–8 distinct candidate sources; 3–4 are encouraged when they test useful alternatives, and a single targeted candidate is valid. Submit each round through the assignment's recorded batch checker. Every candidate is checked independently against the original pack, and every compiler invocation still counts toward the separate compiler budget. Inspect the results before designing the next round. Stop immediately at the first official MATCH. Otherwise preserve the closest actually checked candidate and concise handoff at the attempt limit or lease cutoff.
task_contract.collaboration: You are one of the generalist agents collaborating on this function. The assignment identifies your group, workspace, shared board and shared checker. There are no fixed lead or specialist roles. Collaborate actively: discuss ideas and possible solutions on the shared board, ask each other questions, review other members' candidates and build on useful results. Publish concise observations, candidate source hashes, checked evidence and open questions on the shared board. Distinguish observations from untested hypotheses. Read relevant board entries rather than copying conversation transcripts. Reserve experiments on the board before checking to avoid duplicate work. Do not overwrite another member's files. Use the shared checker for all experiments. The assignment specifies whether the attempt allowance is shared by the team or allocated per member; all members use one controller-owned lease. Preserve complete candidates and concise handoffs. Only the controller may claim, flag, release or submit. A partial improvement is not a match; completion requires the independent original-pack validation gate.
